# odinex_floating_ip (Resource)

Manages a floating IP. Assign it with `server_id` or with `odinex_floating_ip_assignment` (not both).

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "odinex_floating_ip" "web" {
  type          = "ipv4"
  home_location = "fra1"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `type` (String) `ipv4` or `ipv6`.

### Optional

- `delete_protection` (Boolean) Prevent the resource from being deleted. Defaults to `false`.
- `description` (String) Description of the floating IP.
- `home_location` (String) Location of the floating IP. Required unless `server_id` is set.
- `labels` (Map of String) User-defined labels (key/value pairs). Up to 64 pairs; keys and values up to 63 characters.
- `name` (String) Name of the floating IP.
- `server_id` (Number) Server the IP is assigned to.
- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Unique ID of the resource.
- `ip_address` (String) The IP address.

<a id="nestedblock--timeouts"></a>

Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Setting a timeout for a Delete operation is only applicable if changes are saved into state before the destroy operation occurs.
- `update` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import odinex_floating_ip.web 8
```
